newsitem.title: USA: Two lawmakers seek FDA medical device reform.
newsitem.headline: Two lawmakers seek FDA medical device reform.

text.p: A bipartisan pair of lawmakers Thursday introduced a bill to streamline the Food and Drug Administration's regulation of medical devices.
Rep. Joe Barton, a Texas Republican, and Rep. Anna Eshoo, a California Democrat, said their goal was to speed up approval and improve communication between the regulatory agency and the industry.

The bill would make clear when doctors could use devices in clinical trials and or for "compassionate" use. It would also allow manufacturers to make minor changes during a clinical trial without having to start the approval process from scratch.

Devices that do not pose major health questions could be reviewed independently of the FDA, allowing the agency to concentrate on its review of implantable or life-sustaining products. A spokesman for Barton said independent review means private sector reviewers, certified by the FDA, but hired by a the company or manufacturer.

"The FDA approval process -- which is based on law enacted almost 25 years ago - is burdensome, costly and slow," Barton said. "I am concerned that ill patients can wait or possibly even die while life saving devices sit at the FDA."
The Health Industry Manufacturers Association, the major trade group for device makers, praised the bill as a "sound and seasoned approach."
